review.purpose: Select a dialect advertised by the actual shipped rules before correcting text.
review.finding: The released catalog advertises en-US; the notebook materializes available dialects and requires exactly that selected code before proceeding. All later calls explicitly use en-US; availability does not imply appropriateness for all authors.

review.purpose: Retain original text and candidate versions to assess what top-suggestion editing actually changes.
review.finding: The first pass changes eight nonempty drafts from eleven detected matches to three, leaving two flagged drafts and increasing one original count. Version histories preserve exact wording; no monotonic-improvement or preserved-meaning claim is made.

review.purpose: Recheck each materialized candidate rather than treating correction as successful proofreading.
review.finding: The per-draft chart includes zero, reduced and increased counts. One originally single-match draft has two matches after a first fix, demonstrating why a new check is needed. Counts reflect this rule set, not a general quality score.

review.purpose: Interpret the Boolean zero-match flag alongside actual input availability and factual limits.
review.finding: The empty string returns true with count zero, NULL remains NULL, and the intentionally false Moon sentence remains unflagged. Availability is preserved separately and the flag is audited against count=0, not accepted as publication readiness.

review.purpose: Inspect the ordered suggestion and span behind a candidate edit, then reconcile detailed issues with scalar counts.
review.finding: Detailed rows expose the original flagged span, category, rule and suggestions for draft4. Their number matches the original scalar count and UTF16 offsets identify the ASCII text. The subsequent version/count comparison shows that a local suggested fix can expose additional matches.
